Commentary.Commentary: That's a wrap! And the silverware belongs to Sri Lanka! Kusal Mendis proudly lifts the trophy alongside a beaming squad in front of the winners' board, sealing a 1-0 series victory after back-to-back washouts. It's a cruel, bittersweet finale here at the Sabina Park, where the persistent Kingston rain has had the ultimate say, forcing the match officials to call off this final ODI without a single delivery being sent down. While the visitors celebrate, it’s absolute heartbreak for the West Indies. This second consecutive abandonment deals a massive blow to the Men in Maroon and their high-stakes pursuit of automatic World Cup qualification. That wraps up our coverage from the commentary box. Goodbye for now!

The skipper of Sri Lanka - Kusal Mendis said he is delighted to have won the series. He noted that although they played only one match, the team performed well. He added that everyone was keen to get time on the field ahead of the World Cup and play as many matches as possible. He expressed satisfaction with his captaincy in his first series as leader. Mendis also mentioned that they are looking to develop Kamindu Mendis as a top-order batter, praising his solid technique against the new ball. He further highlighted the performances of Pavan Rathnayake, Janith Liyanage, and Milan Rathnayake, who bowled well in the first match. Overall, he said he is pleased with both the batting and bowling units.

The skipper of West Indies - Shai Hope said it was frustrating for the series to end this way. He noted that the team will take lessons from the first game and always aim to be on the winning side, as they can’t change what happened in the last two matches. He added that the team played in patches but still has areas to improve. Hope also credited Sri Lanka for their performance in the opening game. He said the focus now is to look ahead and concentrate on what’s in front of them, as well as to better understand the playing conditions. He mentioned that the players have been together for a while, so it’s about figuring out what they need to do to cross the line against Sri Lanka. He concluded by expressing hope that they can bounce back and turn the series into a winning one.
Presentation time...

The rain wins the day, and the match is officially abandoned due to rain. The umpires felt it would be too slippery to start and the groundstaff simply never stood a chance against this relentless downpour.

UPDATE - 10.32 pm GMT - The drizzle has returned, steady and unrelenting. After a brief break in the clouds, the sky has darkened again, heavy and overcast. In Kingston, rain is expected to persist until midnight. Conditions remain bleak for now, though there is still a chance it may ease later in the night. Fingers crossed for a shortened contest.

UPDATE - 9.39 pm GMT - Rain continues with no change in conditions. The cut-off time for a 20-over-a-side game is 01:02 am GMT. The forecast shows an 85% chance of rain with steady drizzle and strong winds. We’ll have to wait and hope for an improvement before the match can proceed.

UPDATE - 9.28 pm GMT - It’s still raining, but lighter than at toss time. Covers are on, the forecast is poor, and significant effort will be needed to get play. The next update from officials is at 9.30 pm GMT.
UPDATE - 9.10 pm GMT - The rain seems to have eased off, and the puddles that had formed earlier have gone as well. Let's hope the rain goes away completely and the game starts soon.

India’s demolition job in Mullanpur - While we wait for the rain to cease, here is what happened at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium, Mullanpur, New Chandigarh. India completely silenced critics regarding their home form with an emphatic victory over Afghanistan, winning by an innings and 300 runs in under three days. Electing to bat, India piled up a massive 564/8 declared, fueled by superb centuries from KL Rahul and Shubman Gill, despite a fighting six-wicket haul by Saleem Safi. In response, Afghanistan's batting collapsed twice under intense pressure. They were bowled out for 152 in their first innings courtesy of debutant spinner Manav Suthar’s sensational 6/33, and then crumbled for 112 after the follow-on as Washington Sundar and Kuldeep Yadav spun a web around their overly aggressive batting lineup.

UPDATE - 8.25 pm GMT - No new updates at the moment as the rain continues and the covers remain firmly in place. The wind has also picked up over the past few minutes, adding to the challenge. Hopefully, the weather improves soon so play can get underway.
UPDATE - 8 pm GMT - It looks like the rain has eased off, but there are puddles formed on the outfield. The groundstaff will have a massive task on their hands once this finally clears.

UPDATE - 7.20 pm GMT - Rain is now falling more heavily, forcing the players off the field and back into their dressing rooms. More covers have been brought on as conditions continue to deteriorate. Hopefully, the weather clears up soon and play can get underway without much further delay.
UPDATE - 7.05 pm GMT - There is a slight drizzle here at the Sabina Park, and the covers are on. Let's hope it goes away soon. The toss has been delayed due to rain.

Weather could play a decisive role - Adding another layer of intrigue to the contest is the persistent threat of rain. Forecasts suggest overcast conditions once again, raising the possibility of weather interruptions. Will the West Indies rise to the occasion and square the series, or can Sri Lanka complete a memorable 2-0 series win? The answers will unfold shortly, with the toss and team news coming up soon. Stay tuned.

West Indies seek redemption on home soil - Despite several encouraging performances in the first ODI, West Indies ultimately fell 41 runs short. Matthew Forde, Jayden Seales, and Roston Chase impressed with the ball, but costly spells from Alzarri Joseph and Gudakesh Motie helped Sri Lanka reach an above-par total. During the chase, several Windies batters made promising starts, with captain Shai Hope top-scoring with 56. However, the lack of a substantial innings proved costly. With the series at stake, the Men in Maroon will be determined to bounce back and level the contest at 1-1.

Sri Lanka eye series-sealing victory - Sri Lanka delivered a dominant performance in the opening ODI, posting an imposing 303/7. Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka led the charge with impressive half-centuries, while Charith Asalanka and Janith Liyanage provided valuable contributions through the middle order. With the ball, Dushmantha Chameera starred with four wickets, supported effectively by the spin duo of Maheesh Theekshana and Wanindu Hasaranga. Heading into the final ODI, Sri Lanka will be eager to replicate that all-round display and clinch the series.

Series decider set for Sabina Park - Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final ODI between West Indies and Sri Lanka at Sabina Park in Kingston. With the second ODI washed out due to rain, the series reaches its decisive stage. The hosts have an opportunity to draw the series, while the visitors are aiming to secure a commanding 2-0 triumph.
... MATCH DAY ...

The final act - The second ODI at Sabina Park never got beyond the toss as persistent rain washed out the contest, leaving Sri Lanka 1-0 up heading into the series finale.  While the West Indies can no longer win the series, there is still plenty at stake. Valuable ODI World Cup qualification points remain on offer, and the hosts will be desperate to avoid a home series defeat. On the other hand, Sri Lanka are chasing their first bilateral ODI series victory in the Caribbean since 2003. Weather watch - The weather was the winner in the second ODI, with only the toss possible before rain took over. Unfortunately, the forecast for the series decider is not particularly encouraging either. Both teams will be hoping the rain stays away long enough to allow a meaningful contest and a fitting conclusion to the series. West Indies seek answers - The home side continues to search for the right balance. The injury to Matthew Forde meant he was unavailable for the second ODI, and with only a day's gap between matches, his availability remains uncertain. Windies brought in Amir Jangoo to strengthen the batting, and they have now been boosted by the addition of Shimron Hetmyer to the squad. Shai Hope and the Windies think tank have an interesting decision to make regarding who makes way. Beyond personnel, the West Indies will be looking for improvement with the ball. Their inability to apply sustained pressure through the middle overs in the series opener allowed Sri Lanka to seize control, and that remains an area requiring immediate attention. Building on the opener - Sri Lanka's top order was tested early by the West Indies new-ball attack in the first ODI, but the visitors recovered well and gradually lifted the scoring rate as the innings progressed. The challenge will be similar once again, with the Caribbean quicks likely to ask plenty of questions upfront. The tourists' only change for the rain-hit second ODI was the inclusion of Eshan Malinga. Having impressed at the IPL, the 25-year-old seamer will be eager to make his mark should he get an opportunity in the decider. Form (Last 5 completed ODIs, recent first) - WI - LLLLL | SL - WLLWL. What to expect? With overcast conditions expected, seamers are likely to have a major say in the contest. Both sides possess pace attacks with enough quality to exploit any assistance on offer, making the battle with the new ball a potentially decisive phase of the affair. Let's hope for better fortunes this time around in terms of the weather. With ODI World Cup qualification points and a slice of history at stake, the series deserves a fitting conclusion and one that is decided by the players on the field rather than the rain.
